text:
cust_acme: getting 502/504s from the Redwood hosted API starting ~09:02 UTC. Happens on text-generation requests to model 'redwood-3' in us-west-2. Example request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Payload small, not hitting rate limits. Any known issues?

alex_support: sorry about that — can you paste the full request id and any response body you got? Also which account/org?

cust_acme: org: acme-inc; request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Response: HTTP 502 "upstream connect error or disconnect" and then a few 504 timeouts. Not seeing consistent latency spikes from our side.

alex_support: thanks — tagging oncall. @maria_oncall can you take a look? I'll open a ticket INC-2026.

maria_oncall: looking now. I can already see a spike in 5xx for the inference gateway in us-west-2 around 09:02. Attaching recent gateway logs snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T09:02:14Z gateway[gw-3]: upstream request timed out to backend inference-rt-7 (timeout 10s) trace=req_0a1b2c3d
2026-03-15T09:02:15Z cache-proxy[cp-1]: ERROR redis GET kv_prefix:abc123 -> connection refused
2026-03-15T09:02:16Z inference-rt-7: KV cache miss, attempting cold load
2026-03-15T09:02:25Z inference-rt-7: cold start took 13.4s
```

maria_oncall: looks like cache-proxy couldn't reach Redis and the runtime got blocked waiting for KV fetch which cascaded into gateway timeouts.

sam_sre: I see the same in infra metrics — Redis cluster mem-redis-prod-2 reported a rapid drop in available connections and high blocked_clients. Possibly an ACL or partial network partition. Running `redis-cli -h mem-redis-prod-2 -p 6379 INFO` returned: 
```
# Clients
connected_clients:1025
blocked_clients:223
# Persistence
loading:0
# Replication
role:master
connected_slaves:1
# CPU
used_cpu_sys:2345.67
```

sam_sre: also observed lots of `ERR max clients reached` and `LOADING` in older logs.

lee_infra: quick checks: AWS ENI metrics for the redis nodes in az-2 show network errors ~09:01-09:06 and one node had full file descriptors (too many connections). I triggered a failover for the unhealthy node and increased the maxclients parameter on the cluster, plus scaled the read replicas from 2->3.

jordan_engineer: thanks. Root cause hypothesis: cache client retries are aggressive and blocking inference threads while Redis is overloaded; the client doesn't short-circuit quickly enough, so the inference runtime waits and gateway times out. We should add a circuit breaker at cache client level and a short timeout (200-500ms) for prefix KV fetches so work can proceed with cold loads or fall back to local in-memory cache.

alex_support: for the customer: temporary mitigation we applied: scaled Redis replicas and restarted cache-proxy in us-west-2, which restored connections. Can you confirm if you still see errors, @cust_acme?

cust_acme: after ~09:12 we see fewer 5xx. Last error at 09:11:43. Throughput back to normal. Appreciate quick turnaround.

maria_oncall: marking as mitigated in INC-2026 for now. Next steps for engineering: improve cache client resiliency, add non-blocking path for cache misses, and add alerts for blocked_clients > 50%.

jordan_engineer: I'll open a PR with three changes: 
- add 300ms timeout to prefix/KV GETs with immediate fallback
- implement exponential backoff + jitter for cache client retries
- add circuit-breaker that returns a soft-failure to runtime after 2 failed attempts
Link to draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567

sam_sre: also adding infra fix: make maxclients configurable per env and bump default pool to 4096 for prod clusters, plus a small runbook update for failover.

lee_infra: we changed eviction policy to allkeys-lru on the affected cluster and increased ephemeral connection limits on the cache-proxy. Will monitor.

alex_support: notes for customer-facing reply: explain root cause (Redis connection saturation leading to cache-proxy connection refused -> inference timeouts -> gateway 502/504). Apologize, link to INC-2026, and give ETA for engineering fixes (PR and infra changes).

cust_acme: thanks, please keep us posted. Any temporary config we should change on our side?

jordan_engineer: no changes needed on caller side. If you see continued 5xx, collect a request id and timestamp and send to support. Also, if you can avoid bursts that hammer the same prefix keys it helps — we noticed heavy contended prefixes during the event.

deploy-bot: [deploy] cache-proxy/us-west-2 restart initiated by lee_infra at 2026-03-15T09:08:44Z :rocket:

maria_oncall: closing loop here — full postmortem to be posted to #incidents with timeline and action items once Jordan's PR is merged and we've validated infra tweaks.

alex_support: tagging the thread as resolved for now but will reopen if customer reports new errors. :white_check_mark:
